thread:
alejandro: Heads-up — eu-west1 provision pipeline blocked. Several GPU nodes failing attach due to local NVMe issues on scratch devices, causing attach timeouts and node drains.
mika: Details? are these preemptible or dedicated pools? :thinking:
devon: Looks like ephemeral SSDs. IOPS skyrocketing and some blk_update errors in kernel logs. Containers see EIO during image unpack.
alejandro: Preemptible batch pool. Quick paste from dmesg on gnode-ew1-143:

[  123.456789] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[  123.457012] Buffer I/O error on dev nvme0n1p1, logical block 0
[  123.457345] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_da_writepages: jbd2: Detected IO_errors; aborting

mika: ugh. Any pattern on scrub/cleaner overlap times?
alejandro: yes — spike at 03:40 UTC when janitor window overlaps nightly scrub in the region. Cleaner backlog is ~22k files pending.
devon: If cleaner is busy that'll keep io queue full. Can we throttle scrub or pause janitor for affected shards? We need to free attach path for GPUs.
rachel: cost note — pausing scrub increases unit risk but can reduce GPU wait time and on-demand billing. What's the expected recovery time if we pause scrub?
mika: If we pause scrub for 20m and run focused scrubs on hot nodes, we can drop IOPS by ~40% per node. Ops-bot, any recent deploys to janitor?
ops-bot: deploy/janitor/2026-03-21T03:38 completed by ci-cd (sha: b12f9a). No rollbacks.
devon: That deploy changed concurrency default from 8 -> 20 in an attempt to flush backlog faster. Probably made spikes worse.
alejandro: Plan proposal: 1) revert janitor concurrency to 8 on eu-west1 canary shard 2) throttle nightly scrub for 30m across pool 3) drain and reprovision 4 nodes with worst error counts 4) follow-up: add hotspot IO detection to cleaner to adapt concurrency.
mika: +1. I'll run the canary revert now. Command: kubectl -n infra set env deploy/janitor CONCURRENCY=8 --record
mika: also pausing scrub via scheduled job: 
```
# pause scrub window
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/maintenance -d '{"region":"eu-west1","service":"scrub","duration_min":30}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```
devon: I'll start a rolling reprovision for nodes with >5 EIO events:
```
./tools/provision --region eu-west1 --filter 'eio_count>5' --action reprovision --parallel 2
```
alejandro: After revert started, I see IOPS down to baseline on two canaries. One reprovision already completed and GPUs attached successfully.
rachel: Good. Keep an eye on billing delta — if this recurs we'll need scheduler-level backpressure or reduce janitor concurrency permanently in eu-west1.
mika: Filing follow-up ticket for adaptive janitor concurrency + scrub coordination. @sre-runbook can you add runbook steps for future pauses and include cost fallback guidance?
sre-runbook: Yep — will add a short checklist: detection thresholds, quick revert commands, scrub pause endpoint, reprovision command, and postmortem template. ETA 2 hours.
alejandro: Thanks all. Keeping thread open until region stable.
mika: status update in 15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: alert cleared for attach-failure-rate on eu-west1 at 3245681100 (rule: gpu-attach-io-errors)."
